texts.li: {A_nameDef} hummed the same four notes over and over until {B_nameDef} asked whether {A_pronoun} knew any others.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} to stop humming, and {A_nameDef}, still humming, said {A_pronoun} wasn't.
{B_nameDef} snapped at {A_nameDef} that one more hum and {B_pronoun} would go and work somewhere else.
{B_nameDef} started humming along with {A_nameDef}, badly, and it turned into a duet.
{B_nameDef} caught {A_nameDef}'s tune and can't get rid of it, so now they hum it together.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: words spoken in sleep

texts.li: {B_nameDef} repeated word for word what {A_nameDef} had said in {A_possessive} sleep, and {A_nameDef} went red.
{B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, grinning, that {A_pronoun} argues in {A_possessive} sleep with someone called Vera, and loses.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: told what was said in sleep

texts.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef}, cheerfully, how much of the day {B_pronoun} misses by sleeping through the dawn.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} whether {B_pronoun} was only just up, and got asked if {A_pronoun} ever talks about anything but mornings.
{B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} that the food tastes better on the days {A_pronoun} sings while {A_pronoun} cooks.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a recipe, and {A_nameDef} said it only works with the song.
{A_nameDef} tidied {B_nameDef}'s things away while {B_pronoun} was still using them, and stacked them where {B_pronoun} couldn't find them.
{B_nameDef} set a cup down for a moment, and {A_nameDef} had it washed and put away before {B_pronoun} turned round.
{A_nameDef} gave {B_nameDef} a carved spoon, whittled from an offcut over a few evenings.
{A_nameDef} handed {B_nameDef} what {A_pronoun} had been whittling for days, a careful likeness of {B_nameDef}'s favorite animal.
{A_nameDef} knew to the season when {B_nameDef} first came to the colony, and {B_nameDef} was more touched than {B_pronoun} let on.
{A_nameDef} wished {B_nameDef} well for a day that mattered to {B_objective}, and {B_nameDef} had no idea anyone knew.
Last night {A_nameDef} named the stars for {B_nameDef} one by one, and {B_nameDef} suspects half the names were made up.
{A_nameDef} promised to show {B_nameDef} which star is which once it gets dark.
{A_nameDef} counted out loud while {B_nameDef} was trying to think, and started over when {B_nameDef} asked {A_objective} to stop.
{B_nameDef} lost {B_possessive} place three times to {A_nameDef}'s counting, and {A_nameDef} wouldn't stop or say what {A_pronoun} was counting.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} found out they are both superstitious, and compared their precautions at length.
{B_nameDef} saw {A_nameDef}'s ritual and, rather than laugh, showed {A_objective} {B_possessive} own.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued over names for the next animal the colony takes in, and settled on two, one each.
{B_nameDef} has started using the names {A_nameDef} gives the animals, though {B_pronoun} won't admit where they came from.
